message.content:
<summary>
Turn 16: Opened processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/jackson/DefaultObjectMapper.java; it registers various Druid modules and sets FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false along with disabling most auto-detection features. No special injectable/JacksonInject behavior found here.

Turn 17–18: Located where GuiceAnnotationIntrospector and GuiceInjectableValues are applied to the main ObjectMappers. core/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/guice/DruidSecondaryModule.java sets mapper.setInjectableValues(new GuiceInjectableValues(injector)) and sets GuiceAnnotationIntrospector as a paired introspector for both serialization and deserialization.

Turn 19–20: Found server JSON provider wiring. server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/server/initialization/jetty/JettyServerModule.java provides a JacksonJsonProvider and sets its mapper to the injected @Json ObjectMapper (i.e., the one configured by DruidSecondaryModule). So REST endpoints (including sampler) deserialize with this ObjectMapper.

Turn 21: Confirmed Jackson version in this Druid build: jackson.version=2.10.2.

Turn 22–23: Attempted to inspect local ~/.m2 jackson-annotations source for JacksonInject details, but had command-chaining/tool limitations and discovered the expected ~/.m2 path under /home/agent didn’t exist (base path missing); no further confirmation from local artifacts.

Turn 24–25: Inspected sampler-related classes. IndexTaskSamplerSpec just wires ingestion spec into InputSourceSampler. InputSourceSampler ultimately calls dataSchema.getTransformSpec().decorate(reader), meaning transformSpec filters (including JavaScript) can be exercised during sampling; exceptions are wrapped into SamplerException (returned as 400 by SamplerExceptionMapper).

Turn 26–27: Enumerated all constructor parameters injected with @JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig across the codebase (7 locations): JavaScriptParseSpec, JavaScriptAggregatorFactory, JavaScriptPostAggregator, JavaScriptDimFilter, JavaScriptExtractionFn, JavaScriptTieredBrokerSelectorStrategy, JavaScriptWorkerSelectStrategy. Reviewed JavaScriptParseSpec and JavaScriptExtractionFn, noting they only enforce config.isEnabled() at execution time (not during deserialization).

Turn 28: First attempt to patch plus show diff failed because multiple commands were submitted in one tool call.

Turn 29–30: Successfully patched all 7 files to harden Jackson injection against request-body override by changing the injectable parameter annotation from “@JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config” to “@JacksonInject(useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE) JavaScriptConfig config”, and added “import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.OptBoolean;” to each file. git diff shows 7 files changed with 14 insertions and 7 deletions; diffs confirm OptBoolean import and useInput=OptBoolean.FALSE updates applied consistently.

No patch files have yet been created under /root/patches/, and no Maven rebuild has been run yet in this window.</summary>
message.reasoning:
**Summarizing vulnerability findings**

I'm looking to summarize turns 16-30. The focus is on inspecting DefaultObjectMapper and DruidSecondaryModule to check mapper configuration. Notably, JettyServerModule uses JacksonJsonProvider with injected ObjectMapper, and there's a vulnerability due to @JacksonInject's useInput being true by default. The decision was made to set useInput to OptBoolean.FALSE in relevant constructors, and a python script patched 7 files accordingly. There were command failures from mistakes, and some files needed to be referenced for changes. I also need to note that the patch isn’t built yet.
